fullPassage: Skepticism has roots in ancient Greek philosophy, especially in the philosopher Pyrrho of Elis. Pyrrho objected to the dogmatic philosophies of his day, each of which claimed to possess certain knowledge. He questioned whether it was possible for human beings to determine any knowledge with certainty and concluded that we must accept that knowledge always came with uncertainty. To express this consistently, Pyrrho would always preface any claims he made with qualifying phrases like "it seems," "it appears to me," or "perhaps." He taught that this view was also a good way to help humans achieve a sense of inner peace. The citizens of Elis honored his wisdom and made him their head priest. As a bonus, they exempted all philosophers from taxation. Scientists today follow a version of Pyrrho's linguistic practice in the way they, too, use care when making empirical claims by couching them with qualifying phrases to mark their degree of evidential warrant. These may range from verbal indicators of relatively weak evidence that is "suggestive," to indicators of better evidence that makes a conclusion "seem likely," to markers of very strong evidence that allows a conclusion to be drawn with "a high degree of confidence." In any scientific investigation, there are typically several alternative hypotheses that may be in play at any given point in time, and the goal is to sort out their degree of plausibility, eventually eliminating weaker ones, so we may move forward with only the most highly confirmed. The fact that conclusions may achieve higher and higher probability, but never quite reach absolute certainty, is a hallmark of inductive reasoning upon which science is based.

det.tip: preface A with B = A를 B로 시작하다 ≈ introduce

questions.passage: Skepticism has roots in ancient Greek philosophy, especially in the philosopher Pyrrho of Elis. Pyrrho objected to the dogmatic philosophies of his day, each of which claimed to possess certain knowledge. He questioned whether it was possible for human beings to determine any knowledge with certainty and concluded that we must accept that knowledge always came with uncertainty. To express this consistently, Pyrrho would always preface any claims he made with qualifying phrases like "it seems," "it appears to me," or "perhaps." He taught that this view was also a good way to help humans achieve a sense of inner peace. The citizens of Elis honored his wisdom and made him their head priest. As a bonus, they exempted all philosophers from taxation. Scientists today follow a version of Pyrrho's linguistic practice in the way they, too, use care when making empirical claims by couching them with qualifying phrases to mark their degree of evidential warrant. These may range from verbal indicators of relatively weak evidence that is "suggestive," to indicators of better evidence that makes a conclusion "seem likely," to markers of very strong evidence that allows a conclusion to be drawn with "a high degree of confidence." In any scientific investigation, there are typically several alternative hypotheses that may be in play at any given point in time, and the goal is to sort out their degree of plausibility, eventually eliminating weaker ones, so we may move forward with only the most highly confirmed. The fact that conclusions may achieve higher and higher probability, but never quite reach absolute certainty, is a <u>hallmark</u> of inductive reasoning upon which science is based.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 hallmark와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: hallmark는 '전형적 특징, 표징', 즉 characteristic(특징)과 가장 가깝다.
det.analysis:
a hallmark of inductive reasoning = 귀납적 추론의 전형적 특징
② characteristic(특징) — 정답
① exception(예외)은 반대
③ origin(기원) ④ weakness(약점)는 의미가 다름
det.tip: hallmark = 대표적 특징, 상징 ≈ characteristic / feature

questions.passage:
(A) After weighing all the evidence, the jury was finally able to <u>draw</u> a fair conclusion about the case.

(B) The art teacher asked each child to <u>draw</u> a picture of the old stone bridge by the river.
questions.stem: 다음 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 draw의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) draw a conclusion = 결론을 이끌어내다 / (B) draw a picture = 그림을 그리다
det.analysis:
본문 'allows a conclusion to be drawn'의 draw와 같은 뜻은 (A)의 '결론을 이끌어내다'
❌ ① 그림을 그리다 — 이끌어내다 (A와 B가 뒤바뀜)
✅ ② 이끌어내다 — 그림을 그리다 ←정답
❌ ③ 이끌어내다 — 끌어당기다 (B는 '그림을 그리다')
❌ ④ 물을 긷다 — 그림을 그리다 (A는 '결론을 이끌어내다')
det.tip: draw: draw a conclusion(결론을 이끌어내다) vs draw a picture(그림을 그리다)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "an idea that is suggested as a possible explanation for something but has not yet been proven to be true"

det.korean: '아직 증명되지 않은, 가능한 설명으로 제시된 생각' = hypothesis(가설).
det.analysis:
정의: 가능한 설명으로 제시되었지만 아직 참으로 증명되지 않은 생각 → hypothesis
① tradition(전통) — 정의와 무관
② reward(보상) — 무관
③ hypothesis(가설) — 정답. 본문 several alternative hypotheses에서 등장
④ penalty(처벌) — 무관
det.tip: hypothesis(가설) = 아직 증명되지 않은 잠정적 설명

questions.passage: He questioned whether it was possible for human beings to determine any knowledge with certainty and __________ (conclude) that we must accept that knowledge always came with uncertainty.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 앞의 questioned와 등위접속사 and로 병렬을 이루므로 같은 과거시제 concluded가 되어야 한다.
det.analysis: He questioned ... and __________ (conclude) → 주어 He의 과거 동사 두 개가 and로 연결 → 과거시제 concluded
det.tip: conclude(결론짓다) → concluded(과거형): questioned와 병렬

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: '가장 확실히 확인된 것들(the most highly confirmed ones)'이라는 수동·완료의 의미이므로 과거분사 confirmed가 되어야 한다.
det.analysis: the most highly __________ (confirm) → 명사를 수식하는 과거분사(수동: 확인된) → confirmed
det.tip: confirm(확인하다) → confirmed(확인된, 과거분사): 수동의 의미
